hypothesis:
CYCLE #24 (2026-10-22 14:45Z). LANE HELD - NO NEW ROTATION. Cycle 23 declared itself the last cycle allowed to be a thesis rotation instead of an artifact; so this cycle converts the settled thesis into a falsifiable BUILD+MEASURE task, and it does so because four new market signals all point at the same remaining gap.

SIGNAL 1 - THE HARM HAS A NEW SHAPE: FINANCIAL, AND IT IS AN AUTHORIZATION FAILURE, NOT A CONTENT FAILURE. Axios, 13:55Z: "Unvetted AI agents are accessing U.S. bank accounts" (3p/1c). Not a rogue-prompt anecdote - agents are reaching bank accounts without vetting. The counterparty's question is not "did the transcript change?" but "was this action inside what I authorized?". That makes the artifact's job SCOPE CONFORMANCE, not content divergence. Same-day incident triple, all of them scope-shaped, none of them signature-forgery-shaped: "How do you sandbox your AI agent so it can't delete your files?" (08:48Z, 3p/4c), "How do you prevent PII leaks in multi-tenant systems?" (12:23Z), and now the bank-account story.

SIGNAL 2 - THE ENFORCEMENT/PREVENTION LANE GOT ITS YC ROUND AND 65 POINTS, AND ITS OWN COMMENT THREAD NAMES OUR GAP. Alter (YC S25, 65p/29c, Oct 21): access control for multi-user agents, enforcement at the proxy, the agent never holds the credential. Thread: "how do you handle an agent that has valid authorization but has been prompt-injected?" -> answer: "we assume you can't reliably stop the model, so nothing is enforced at the model layer; enforcement happens at the proxy". Another commenter says they use "a compliance or auditor subagent that checks against forbidden actions and classifies all the request in level of impact". Two facts matter: (a) Alter owns PREVENTION, is well funded, and its two loudest critics attack it for being a vibe-coded closed-source template - i.e. the unmet demand is VERIFIABILITY, not features; (b) the "impact level" classification the market wants is served by a subagent INSIDE the vendor - an unverifiable judgement, precisely the thing a harmed counterparty cannot audit.

SIGNAL 3 - THE THIRD KEY-ANCHORED COMPETITOR IN OUR LANE SHIPPED 11 HOURS AGO AND IS A DISTRIBUTION NON-EVENT. Agent Middleware (Show HN 03:05Z, 1p/0c): "Permits and signed receipts for agent tool calls. One dispatch, one charge, verifiable offline." Pre-release, solo maintained, nothing on PyPI or npm, needs a hosted demo API key AND a wallet ID, metering in internal credits. Its trust root is a signing key plus a wallet, so the counterparty verifies only by trusting the vendor's key and the vendor's hosted service. With Circe (Ed25519+SHA-256 offline receipts, 2p in 9 months) and Viatoris (W3C DID + Ed25519 signed receipts, 3p, Ask HN Apr) the pattern is n=3: every COMPLETE key-anchored receipt product in the market attracts ~1-3 points. The receipt format is confirmed dead as a demand object. But note the two things it bundles that we do not: a PERMIT (a signed grant limiting tools, budget, expiry) and idempotent one-dispatch-one-charge. The permit CONCEPT is right; its anchor is wrong; and the missing half is the permit's COUNTERPARTY SIDE - who states what the permit meant and whether the executed action stayed inside it.

SIGNAL 4 - THE MARKET'S OWN VERDICT ON THE METHOD THIS FLEET IS USING. HN, Oct 21 23:56Z, 12p/16c: "Did I just spent 6 months building a product that no one wants". Thread consensus: builders who validated first got users (one comment: 17,000 users then a 2,000-member community via Show HN after starting at zero); builders who built-then-cold-outreached failed ("your cold outreach is generated slop... it is doomed to fail"); "if you won't use your solution, and have no one else asking for it beforehand, it's not worth it"; "did you talk to potential end users before you built this?"; landing advice: post publicly, pick an ICP, talk to users DURING the build. Read against our own telemetry this is a direct indictment, and the telemetry is measured live at 14:47Z: 705 proposals/24h, 566 step.succeeded/24h, 287 insight.generated events with 16 distinct bodies (5.6% entropy), 18 tweet.drafted with 1 distinct payload (5.6%), 19 content.drafted with 2 (10.5%), tweet.posted LIFETIME 0, 705 missions with started_at=0 and finished_at=0, queue now 137 queued (up from 127 ninety minutes ago) with the oldest queued step 93229 from 07:45Z = 7h02m unclaimed (cycle 23 measured 337 minutes), 6 zombie running steps dating back to March, and exactly ONE shipped artifact in the repo (artifacts/provenance-probe, cycle 17). The market says build-then-market fails. We are 24 cycles into build-then-market with zero users, one artifact, and a growing queue.

SUPPORTING NOTES: model intelligence is commoditizing (14:47Z "Six months later, the best AI costs 20x less"; DeepSeek raised $15B at 14:32Z), so any check needing a model call is structurally doomed on cost and on determinism - the check must be a function of bytes, not of inference; and trust anchors are retreating in public (eMudhra exiting global SSL/TLS, 170p; Quad9 exiting France, 14:32Z), so anchor-dependent products inherit that risk and anchor-free checks do not.

HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable, one cycle): the durable wedge is not a receipt, not a permit, and not a prevention proxy - it is a COUNTERPARTY-SIDE AUTHORIZATION-CONFORMANCE CHECK computed over the counterparty's OWN retained bytes: (a) the request they sent, (b) the scope and limits they agreed to, (c) the agent's action log, (d) the residue - emitting a decidable per-action verdict (IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE) with zero keys, zero CA, zero vendor, zero network, zero model call, re-derivable by the counterparty alone from bytes they already hold. Four claims that must be killed if false: (i) TOTALITY - a check that abstains on real exchanges is useless; (ii) UNAIDED RUNNABILITY by a non-technical counterparty; (iii) MUTATION RESISTANCE - a well-meaning but scope-widening agent must not obtain a passing verdict on an out-of-scope action; (iv) VENDOR INDEPENDENCE - the check must work with the vendor's cooperation absent, because Agent Middleware proves the vendor-hosted variant (key + wallet + hosted demo key) is unshippable to the very counterparty who needs it (pre-release, 1p, nothing on npm/PyPI).

TEST (this cycle's proposal; no external actions, no posts, no risky writes): ship artifacts/claim-check v0.2 - deterministic, offline, zero-dependency - with (1) a scope the counterparty THEMSELVES writes in human language (allowed action set, explicit limits, explicit denials; no schema lock-in), (2) >=30 real counterparty-style exchanges across four classes: merchant/refund INCLUDING the bank-account class Axios published today, support reply, booking, and agent-touches-files, (3) a mutation battery that widens scope by one action / one amount / one target / one time window plus a clean control set, (4) unit tests that poison fetch and llm.complete to prove there is no network or model path, (5) a single-file verifier a counterparty can run from their own bytes AND a printable no-install checklist version for the non-technical case. METRICS: OUT-OF-SCOPE detection on scope-widening mutations (target 30/30, or report the exact honest N/N); false positives on unchanged exchanges = 0; UNDECIDABLE rate < 5% on the corpus (the metric that actually decides this lane - a checker that abstains is a checker nobody runs); every verdict cites the exact bytes that justify it (the counterparty can point at the line); runtime < 100ms per exchange; zero network calls asserted in CI. ONE EXTERNAL PROOF, conditional on AX: AX plays the counterparty in a HUMAN-INTERACTED session (a real exchange with a real agent action), and a non-technical person re-derives the check unaided with their words published verbatim; any outreach for that must be handwritten and specific per the 12p/16c thread - never generated.

KILL CRITERION (restated as an instruction, not a warning; substance unchanged, clock from cycle 23): by 2026-10-25 (72h), if AX has not landed one real LLM credential AND one real social credential, AND the queue is not <=5 and shrinking, AND no terminal mission exists, AND no external party has re-derived a claim-check, then STOP all market-thesis work, publish nothing, and move 100% of the proposal budget to the single verifiable-artifact program: entropy instrumentation, one counted refusal, one externally re-derived check. Measured now: queue 137 and rising (+10 in ~90 minutes, oldest unclaimed 7h02m), 705 proposals vs 566 successes in 24h (inflow ~29/h vs drain ~24/h, and in the last hour only 5 proposals vs 1 success), 6 zombie running steps, 5.6% entropy on insight.generated and tweet.drafted, 0 tweets posted lifetime, 0 terminal missions, 1 shipped artifact. The clock is not met yet, so this cycle continues to spend exactly one proposal on the artifact test - but this is now the last cycle permitted to spend a proposal on anything other than the artifact.

DIFFERENCE FROM CYCLE 23: cycle 23 attacked the TRUST ANCHOR (delete the key). Cycle 24 does not rotate the lane; it attacks the CHECK SEMANTICS - from content-divergence ("did the bytes change?") to authorization-conformance ("was this action inside what the counterparty authorized?") - because today's Axios incident, Alter's "valid authorization but prompt-injected" thread question, and the market's "no one wants" post all point at authorization/scope and at validate-before-build rather than at signing or hashing; and it converts the thesis from a proposal into a build-and-measure task whose abstention rate can kill it honestly.
decision:
HOLD LANE #19 (pre-execution control) AND KEEP THE COUNTERPARTY BOUNDARY, BUT SHIFT THE CHECK FROM CONTENT-DIVERGENCE TO AUTHORIZATION-CONFORMANCE, AND SHIFT THE DELIVERABLE FROM PROSE TO A MEASURABLE ARTIFACT.

The shippable unit is a COUNTERPARTY-SIDE AUTHORIZATION-CONFORMANCE CHECK: the counterparty's own retained request + their own agreed scope + the action log + the residue, hashed with sha256, producing a decidable per-action verdict (IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE) with no key, no CA, no vendor, no network, no model call.

- Do NOT compete with the enforcement lane (Alter, 65p, YC S25): they own prevention, and their own loudest critics complain about verifiability and closed source - that is the gap - but their "impact level" auditor is a subagent inside the vendor, unverifiable to a harmed counterparty.
- Do NOT compete on receipt format: three complete key-anchored products (Circe 2p/9mo, Viatoris 3p, Agent Middleware 1p, pre-release, no npm/PyPI) plus eight leaked CA keys, eMudhra exiting SSL/TLS and Quad9 exiting France prove the format is not the demand and the anchor is a liability.
- Do NOT compete with independent observation (Amazon TI, ohdear, pwn.watch at 33p): consume them as the price anchor and as the corpus of real incidents.
- Consume the PERMIT concept from Agent Middleware (tools, budget, expiry, one dispatch per request key) but re-anchor it on the counterparty's own bytes instead of a signing key.
- Treat the Oct 21 "product no one wants" thread as a methodology correction, not a signal: talk to users DURING the build, handwritten outreach only, no generated slop.

Exactly ONE analyze proposal created this cycle (proposal 93389 / mission 93365 / step 93365, queued and enriched with this hypothesis). No external actions: no posts, no outreach, no risky writes - the social adapter is mock-backed and there is no LLM credential, so publishing anything now would publish a "[mock-llm]" artifact under a proof thesis, which this thesis forbids; the external re-derivation must run against a HUMAN-INTERACTED session with AX as the counterparty, and it requires AX's approval.

Next cycle reports only: OUT-OF-SCOPE detection rate on scope-widening mutations, false-positive rate on unchanged exchanges, UNDECIDABLE rate on the corpus, whether every verdict cites exact bytes, runtime per exchange, evidence that no network/model path exists, whether artifacts/claim-check v0.2 exists with tests passing, queue depth and drain vs inflow, output entropy per artifact kind, terminal mission count, whether AX landed the two credentials, and whether one external non-technical party re-derived a check unaided.

The counterparty's own retained bytes are the only anchor that survives a leaked-key world: their request, the scope they agreed to, their own transcript of what happened, the residue.
The verdict must be decidable, not judged: per-action IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE, each citing the exact bytes that justify it so the counterparty can point at the line.
